movement_source: row 'CET1 capital ratio (Level 2, APRA Group)', column As at 30 Sept 2024 -> column As at 30 Sept 2025
headline: Westpac's APRA Level 2 CET1 capital ratio rose 4 bps to 12.53% at 30 September 2025 from 12.49% at 30 September 2024. The increase was driven by net profit accumulation and other reserve movements (including lower capitalised software balances), partially offset by higher total RWA ($12.6 billion increase, mainly from IRRBB RWA) and on-market share buybacks. The internationally comparable CET1 ratio moved 1 bps to 18.28%. No full-year CET1 walk chart is published; the bank provides only a half-on-half (Mar-25 to Sep-25) walk showing +80 bps from net profit, −58 bps from dividends, −7 bps from RWA, +16 bps from capital deductions/other items, and −2 bps from capital return.

drivers.narrative: Net profit accumulated over FY25 supported the CET1 ratio. The bank states the increase came from 'net profit' (results announcement p28). For the half-on-half period (context), net profit contributed +80 bps (ev-24). The bank does not disclose a specific bps impact for the full year.

Payment of the 2024 final ordinary dividend (76 cps) and the 2025 interim ordinary dividend (76 cps) reduced CET1. The bank states these payments were part of the offsetting factors (p28). For the half-on-half period, the 1H25 dividend reduced the ratio by 58 bps (ev-25). DRP for the final dividend is satisfied via third-party market purchases, not new issuance.

Total RWA increased by $12.6 billion (3%) to $450.0 billion, mainly from higher IRRBB RWA (+33% to $37.3 billion). Credit RWA rose $1.2 billion: +$12.6b from higher lending in Corporate and Large Corporate, partly offset by -$5.9b from model updates and data refinements, -$3.0b from improved delinquency rates, -$1.8b from FX translation, and -$0.8b from CVAs (ev-13 through ev-17). Non-credit RWA fell $0.7 billion, with IRRBB RWA down $2.0 billion (ev-19 through ev-21). The bank states higher Total RWA offset the CET1 increase (p28).

Other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances increased CET1. The bank states these were part of the positive drivers (p28). For the half-on-half period, capital deductions and other items contributed +16 bps (ev-27). The bank does not disclose a specific bps impact for the full year.

On-market share buybacks reduced CET1. The bank states buybacks were an offsetting factor (p28). For the half-on-half period, capital return (buyback) reduced the ratio by 2 bps (ev-28). The investor discussion pack notes a remaining on-market buyback previously announced in Nov-23, May-24 and Nov-24 (p77).

limitations: No primary (FY24→FY25) CET1 walk chart is published by Westpac. Only half-on-half (Mar-25→Sep-25) walks are available in both the results announcement (p29) and investor discussion pack (p77). Per task instructions, those context-chart bars cannot be used as FY24→FY25 driver contributions.

The bank's full-year narrative (p28) identifies the direction of each driver qualitatively but does not quantify bps impacts for the FY24→FY25 comparison. All quantified bps figures in this attribution come from the half-on-half walk and are described in narratives as context for that different period.
The residual equals the full movement (4 bps) because no quantified drivers sum to it — this reflects the absence of a primary walk rather than unexplained variance.
The internationally comparable CET1 ratio (18.27% → 18.28%, +1 bps) is a different measure and is reported as context only (ev-6).
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.
No published walk covers FY25 vs FY24: the bank's walk for this metric describes another comparison, so the driver split is not walk-verified for this comparison. Confidence is capped at 85.

The Level 2 CET1 capital ratio was 12.53% at 30 September 2025, 4 basis points higher than 30 September 2024. The increase from net profit less the payment of 2024 final ordinary dividend and 2025 interim ordinary dividend, other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances was offset by higher Total RWA and on market share buybacks. Total RWA increased by $12.6 billion mainly from higher Interest Rate Risk in the banking book (IRRBB) RWA.

- Internationally comparable 18.28% 18.27% 1 bps

Total RWA increased by 0.1% to $450.0 billion over the half from higher credit RWA partly offset by lower non-credit RWA.

Total RWA increased by 0.1% to $450.0 billion over the half from higher credit RWA partly offset by lower non-credit RWA.
Credit RWA increased by $1.2 billion. Key movements included:
A $12.6 billion increase from higher lending primarily in Corporate and Large Corporate;
A $5.9 billion decrease from model updates, methodology and policy changes and other data refinements mainly in RBNZ Regulated Entities and Corporate;
A $3.0 billion decrease mainly due to improvements in residential mortgages delinquency rates;
A $1.8 billion decrease from foreign currency translation impacts, predominantly the appreciation of the AUD against the NZD; and
A $0.8 billion decrease from credit valuation adjustments.
Non-credit RWA decreased by $0.7 billion. Key movements included:
IRRBB RWA: $2.0 billion decrease from:
A $1.2 billion net decrease across repricing and yield curve, basis and optionality risk in line with underlying banking book positions; and
A $0.8 billion decrease from lower interest rates resulting in the regulatory embedded gain increasing to $3.9 billion
Market RWA: $1.4 billion increase mainly from higher market risk exposures
The Level 2 CET1 capital ratio at 30 September 2025 was 12.53%, 29 basis points higher than 31 March 2025. Key movements included:
Second Half 2025 net profit: 80 basis points increase;
Payment of the 2025 interim ordinary dividend: 58 basis points reduction;
RWA movement: 7 basis points decrease mainly from higher credit RWA partly offset by lower non-credit RWA;
Capital deductions and other items: 16 basis points increase mainly from other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances; and
Capital return: 2 basis points reduction due to the on market share buyback.
